title: Sindhu Is the Third Seed in Sydney. Sen and Srikanth Are Not There. Satwik Is Injured.
excerpt: PV Sindhu leads a 24-member Indian contingent at the Australian Open as India's top men's players sit out and a new generation steps up.
body:
She has not won a BWF World Tour title since the Syed Modi International in December 2024. She reached the semifinals of the Malaysia Open earlier this year and exited before the quarterfinals in two other tournaments. For PV Sindhu, the 2026 season has been one of those years where the results do not match the effort — close but never quite there.

On Tuesday, she gets another chance. The Australian Open Super 500 begins in Sydney, and Sindhu is the third seed in the women's singles draw, one of the favourites to win the title, and the undisputed leader of a 24-member Indian contingent that is both depleted and ambitious.

## Who Is Missing — and Why It Matters

The absences are significant. Lakshya Sen, who won this tournament last year, is not defending his title. Kidambi Srikanth, the 2017 champion, is also missing. Neither absence has been fully explained, but the effect is clear: India's men's singles challenge at the Quaycentre in Sydney's Olympic Park rests on 21-year-old Ayush Shetty, who is seeded sixth after breaking into the world's top twenty, and on the experienced HS Prannoy, who has been a reliable performer on the World Tour for the better part of a decade.

The bigger blow came in men's doubles. Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, India's highest-ranked pair and Asian Games gold medallists, pulled out after Satwik sustained a shoulder injury during the Indonesia Open last week. Their absence leaves Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun as India's lead doubles pair — the same duo who reached their first-ever BWF Super 1000 quarterfinal in Jakarta just days ago.

India will have no representation in women's doubles at all.

## Sindhu's Draw and the Road Ahead

Sindhu opens against Peru's Ines Lucia Castillo, a qualifier-level opponent who should not cause trouble. A potential second-round match against fellow Indian Isharani Baruah would be more interesting — Baruah has been a steady presence on the domestic circuit — but the real tests lie further ahead. A semifinal against Japan's Akane Yamaguchi, one of the most technically complete players in the world, and a possible final against Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong are the kind of matches that have tripped Sindhu up in recent months.

She is 31 now. The two Olympic medals — silver in Rio, bronze in Tokyo — are not going anywhere, but the hunger for titles has not diminished. A win in Sydney would be her first Super 500 title in over eighteen months and a statement that she remains India's best bet in women's singles heading into the back half of the Olympic cycle.

## The Young Guns

This tournament is as much about who India is building as it is about who India already has. Shetty, the Mangaluru-born left-hander, has been the breakout story of Indian badminton in 2026. He reached the pre-quarterfinals of the Indonesia Open, the toughest draw on the World Tour, and carries a game that combines deceptive net play with explosive rear-court attacking. He opens against a qualifier in Sydney.

Kiran George and Tharun Mannepalli round out the men's singles contingent. Neither is seeded, but both are capable of an upset in the early rounds.

In women's singles, Sindhu is joined by six other Indians who have earned direct entry into the main draw: Malvika Bansod, Anmol Kharb, Tanvi Sharma, Aakarshi Kashyap, Tanya Hemanth, and Isharani Baruah. Imad Farooqui Samiya will compete in qualifying. It is the deepest Indian women's singles contingent at a Super 500 event in recent memory.

In mixed doubles, Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto will carry India's hopes. The pair has shown flashes of world-class ability but has not yet put together a deep run at a major tournament.

## The NRI Viewing Guide

For the Indian diaspora in Australia — and Sydney has one of the largest Indian communities outside the subcontinent — this is a rare chance to watch top-level Indian badminton live. The Quaycentre at Sydney Olympic Park is accessible by train and bus from most parts of the city, and tickets are typically affordable for a Super 500 event.

For those elsewhere, live streaming is available on the BWF YouTube channel for the early rounds. JioHotstar will broadcast the later stages in India. With the first matches starting Tuesday morning Sydney time — late Monday night in the United States — diaspora fans on the American East Coast will need to stay up past midnight for the first-round action.

## Schedule

The Australian Open 2026 runs from June 9 to June 14 in Sydney.

- **June 9-10:** First round
- **June 11:** Round of 16
- **June 12:** Quarterfinals
- **June 13:** Semifinals
- **June 14:** Finals

*All matches are played at the Quaycentre, Sydney Olympic Park.*
